title: June SOI gave no clear added autumn DMI forecast skill beyond sea temperature and trend in 1981-2024
abstract: We tested whether June Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) adds autumn Indian Ocean Dipole Mode Index (DMI) forecast skill beyond June DMI, June Nino 3.4 and a linear time trend. Each fit used earlier annual targets only, from 1951. For 44 forecasts in 1981-2024, adding SOI reduced mean squared error by 8.15%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -26.37% to 28.49%. Root mean squared error fell from 0.316 to 0.303 degrees C. The test gives no clear added June skill. A planned May check gave a 15.10% reduction, with limits of 1.51% to 27.06%, before adjustment for multiple checks. This secondary result needs a separate test. Revised data, one model form and a short record limit use. The result does not show that atmospheric coupling has no forecast value. Code, aggregate scores, source hashes, a numerical audit and a figure are included. Source records and generated annual tables remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Added SOI forecast error reduction and conditional 95% intervals. June is the primary test. May is a secondary check. Positive values mean lower error. All model variants and scoring checks are shown.

citations.reason: Published June DMI forecast and trend control motivate this atmospheric index test. The source data overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
